data.name: Saketha
data.gender_notes: Saketha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Satya’, meaning truth, Saketha is a feminine name in Hindu mythology, representing the goddess of truth, virtue, and morality. She is also known as ‘Saketamata’, and is often invoked for truth and honesty. The name Saketha carries the meaning “Lord of Truth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Saketha usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Saketha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Truth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saketha total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Naming a child Saketha is a constant reminder for them to uphold these virtues in their lives and actions. Aside from this, the name carries a rich and deep history, rooted in Hindu mythology and its reverence for truth and morality.
